prompt:
In pea plants, purple flower color ($P$) is dominant to white flower color ($p$). Two heterozygous purple-flowered plants are crossed: $Pp \times Pp$.

What percentage of the offspring is expected to have white flowers?
teacher_notes: Ask a follow-up about why an actual cross of twelve offspring may not show exactly three purple to one white.
explanation: A $Pp \times Pp$ cross produces the genotypes $PP$, $Pp$, $Pp$, and $pp$ in equal proportions. Only the homozygous recessive $pp$ genotype produces white flowers, so 1 of 4, or $25\%$, is expected. This is a probability for a large sample, not a guarantee for any single litter of offspring.
